title: Dub a film into English in each actor's own voice
summary: A developer built a setup where Claude Code or Codex dubs films in each actor's copied voice; he reports watchable results, with a full movie taking about seven hours.
agent_role: The agent works out who says each line, corrects speech-recognition errors, writes translations timed to each actor, triages QA flags and re-renders problem lines. The human listens, judges acting and mix, and asks for fixes.
outcome: Author reports watchable dubs, with a full movie in both voices taking about seven hours of machine time on a laptop RTX 4090.
what_they_did: A developer spent weeks writing scripts and an instruction file so a coding agent can dub a video. Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can run it. The setup splits the video and separates voices from music. It writes out the speech with Whisper, a speech-to-text tool, plus two backups. It matches each line to a speaker using voice and video frames. The agent then fixes, translates and times every line. Each line is spoken in a copied voice, mixed in, then turned back into text to check.
how_it_went: The author shares demos of a Japanese anime and a Japanese film dubbed into English. A short clip takes minutes. A full movie in both voices takes about seven hours of computer time on a laptop with a powerful RTX 4090 graphics card. Using only the actor's voice takes about half that.
worth_knowing: The agent can't hear, so you must judge the voices and the mix yourself. A movie used about 85 GB of disk space until cleanup. Only dub videos you have rights to, and copy voices only with consent.
prompt: Using the dub-anything repo and its AGENTS.md, dub [path to video file] from [source language] into [target language]. First confirm the setup is installed and ask me which voice option I want. Show me the cast list and any lines you are unsure about before rendering the full dub. When finished, give me the dubbed file and a list of timestamps I should listen to and check.

curation.rationale: A novel use with real depth: a coding agent directs a full local dubbing pipeline line by line, including casting, translation timing and QA. It comes with code, demos, detailed docs and stated machine-time costs.
